title: B1 · L4 — Past perfect continuous
description: El past perfect continuous ('had been + verbo-ing') expresa duración de una acción hasta un punto específico del pasado o explica una situación pasada visible.

questions.prompt: Cuentas por qué tu compañera estaba agotada al llegar la mañana siguiente.
questions.question: Complete: 'She was tired because she ___ all night.'
questions.explanation: 'Had been working' (past perfect continuous) enfatiza la DURACIÓN de una acción anterior que explica un estado pasado. Contraste: 'had worked' solo dice que trabajó; 'had been working' subraya que estuvo largo rato haciéndolo. Error típico: usar past continuous ('was working'), que no relaciona con el cansancio posterior.
examples: He was drenched in sweat because he'd been running for an hour. → causa prolongada
Her eyes were puffy because she'd been crying all morning. → estado + proceso anterior

questions.statement: 'Had been + -ing' is used to emphasise how long an action had lasted up to a point in the past.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. El past perfect continuous se enfoca en la DURACIÓN de una acción anterior hasta un momento pasado, o en el EFECTO visible que produjo. Es el equivalente pasado del present perfect continuous, corriendo un tiempo hacia atrás.
examples: By 2020, they'd been living there for a decade. → duración hasta un punto pasado
I'd been studying for hours when she called. → duración + evento interruptor

questions.prompt: Llegas a casa y encuentras a los niños pegados a la pantalla.
questions.question: Choose: 'When I got home, the kids ___ TV for hours.'
questions.explanation: 'For hours' + acción prolongada hasta tu llegada → past perfect continuous. 'Were watching' (past continuous) solo describe lo que hacían, sin la idea de 'llevar horas'. 'Had watched' (simple) sonaría como un balance de programas terminados, no continuidad.
examples: When he arrived, I'd been waiting for two hours — I was furious. → duración anterior
By dinner time, they'd been playing for hours. → tiempo acumulado hasta el punto

questions.text: He had been living in Berlin for ten years before he moved back home.
questions.explanation: Nota la contracción típica: 'He'd been living...'. La 'd' de 'had' se pega al pronombre y casi desaparece. 'For ten years' se enlaza como 'for-ten-years' sin pausa. Estructura clásica de biografía: 'had been + -ing + for + periodo + before + past simple'.
examples: She'd been teaching for 20 years before she retired. → biografía profesional
They'd been dating for five years before they got engaged. → hito relacional

questions.prompt: Identifica la única frase gramaticalmente correcta.
questions.question: Which sentence uses past perfect continuous correctly?
options: I had been eaten a lot.
She has been waiting an hour.
They had been studying for three hours when the teacher arrived.
questions.explanation: La estructura correcta es 'had been + verbo-ing'. Errores: (a) 'been eaten' es voz pasiva, no continuous; (b) present perfect continuous, no past perfect; (d) mezcla imposible 'was been'. Solo la opción 3 encaja: duración hasta un punto pasado.
examples: We'd been driving for hours when we finally stopped for coffee. → duración + interrupción
She'd been feeling ill all week before she saw a doctor. → estado prolongado anterior

questions.prompt: Empareja concepto con ejemplo o descripción:

pairs.right: The road was wet because it had been raining.

questions.explanation: El past perfect continuous se centra en duración o efectos visibles de una acción anterior. Como todas las formas continuas, evita verbos de estado (know, own, believe, understand) — con estos usa past perfect simple.
examples: I'd been reading for hours when the phone rang. → duración interrumpida
The floor was muddy because the dog had been running in the garden. → resultado visible

questions.prompt: Sales a la calle y el suelo está encharcado.
questions.question: Complete: 'The ground was wet because it ___ heavily.'
questions.explanation: El estado pasado (wet) se explica por una acción prolongada anterior. Past perfect continuous es la elección natural para enfatizar el proceso. 'Had rained' (simple) sería más neutro; 'had been raining' pinta la imagen de lluvia continua durante rato.
examples: The pavement was slippery because it had been snowing all night. → proceso prolongado
His voice was hoarse because he'd been shouting at the game. → causa prolongada

questions.target: I'd been working there for about five years before I finally decided to change jobs.
questions.explanation: Situación: cuentas tu historia laboral en una entrevista o coffee chat. Estructura clave: 'had been + -ing + for + periodo + before + past simple'. Contracción 'I'd' obligatoria en habla natural. 'About' suaviza la cifra; 'finally' añade emoción a la decisión.
examples: I'd been studying English for three years before I moved abroad — huge step. → antecedente + decisión
She'd been living alone for a while before she got a flatmate, actually. → duración + cambio

questions.statement: 'I had been knowing him for years' is a correct English sentence.
questions.explanation: FALSO. 'Know' es verbo de estado → NO admite forma continua. Lo correcto: 'I had known him for years' (past perfect simple). Este error es TOP-3 en hispanohablantes porque 'conocer' en español puede parecer un proceso. Otros verbos con la misma trampa: love, hate, own, believe, understand.
examples: I'd known him for years before we became business partners. → verbo de estado en simple
She'd owned that car for a decade before selling it. → 'own' nunca en continuous

questions.prompt: Compara qué opción enfatiza mejor la duración hasta un punto pasado.
questions.question: Which best emphasises duration up to a past point?
options: I had studied for three hours.
I had been studying for three hours.
I was studying for three hours.
questions.explanation: 'I had been studying for three hours' es la forma canónica para duración continua hasta un momento pasado. 'Had studied' (simple) da un balance completo; 'was studying' solo describe la acción en un momento; 'studied' es solo pasado neutro sin conexión.
examples: By 6 p.m., I'd been working for eight hours straight — brutal. → duración hasta punto
By midnight, we'd been talking for hours and hours. → tiempo acumulado prolongado

questions.prompt: Cuentas una anécdota sobre esperar el autobús bajo la lluvia.
questions.question: Complete: 'They ___ for the bus for 30 minutes when it finally arrived.'
questions.explanation: La acción de esperar comenzó antes de la llegada y siguió hasta ese momento. Past perfect continuous captura la duración vivida. 'Had waited' (simple) sería aceptable pero menos vívido. 'Were waited' es voz pasiva imposible aquí.
examples: We'd been standing in line for an hour when the doors finally opened. → espera vívida
I'd been trying to fix it for ages when he arrived — perfect timing. → duración + evento

questions.text: By the time she quit, she had been feeling unhappy at work for months.
questions.explanation: Nota el weak form de 'had been' — casi se traga en habla natural ('she'd been feelin'). 'By the time' se pronuncia como una sola unidad rítmica. Estructura útil para explicar decisiones basadas en situaciones prolongadas: 'By the time + past simple + past perfect continuous'.
examples: By the time she called, I'd been sleeping for two hours — completely out. → interrupción
By the time we left the restaurant, they'd been arguing for a while. → tensión previa

questions.statement: Past perfect continuous can only describe activities, not states.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Como toda forma continua, el past perfect continuous solo funciona con verbos dinámicos (activities): run, work, study, wait, play. Con verbos de estado (know, own, believe) usa past perfect simple. Cuidado: algunos verbos como 'feel' o 'live' admiten ambas formas según el matiz.
examples: He'd been running for hours. → actividad dinámica
He'd known me for years. → estado, forma simple obligatoria

questions.prompt: Ves a tu prima cubierta de harina al entrar en la cocina.
questions.question: Choose the best option: 'She was covered in flour because she ___ a cake.'
questions.explanation: Estado visible ('covered in flour') + causa prolongada anterior → past perfect continuous. Foco en el proceso que dejó la evidencia. 'Had made' (simple) sonaría como pastel terminado; 'was making' solo describe lo que hacía en ese instante, sin conectar con el estado.
examples: He was covered in paint because he'd been painting the fence all day. → causa visible
She was out of breath because she'd been dancing non-stop. → efecto físico

questions.target: I'd been trying to learn the guitar for months before I finally gave up — it just wasn't for me.
questions.explanation: Situación: hablas de proyectos personales abandonados en una charla casual. Combina past perfect continuous (duración del intento) con past simple (decisión definitiva). Contracción 'I'd' + discourse marker 'finally' + cierre honesto son muy naturales. Frase típica para hablar de metas frustradas.
examples: She'd been dieting for weeks before she decided to stop, honestly. → proceso + decisión
We'd been saving for years before we bought the house — worth every penny. → esfuerzo prolongado + logro
